homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym, and T composes no other entity under the name: cards 2 and 3 are the archive's own podcast and card 4 its own Mastodon account (its website link verified to leftarchive.ie). 'ILA', the census's short name, is not used as an alias (too short to match only the entity). The Irish Left Online Document Archive (the 2007 name) and the CLR Irish Left Archive (clririshleftarchive.org, the former address, which redirects) are the entity's own earlier names. The distinct entities below are named by the field or the census beside the entity and are never senses of its name.
distinct_entities: the Cedar Lounge Revolution (cedarlounge.wordpress.com), the left blog that initiated and hosts it and on which documents continue to be posted and discussed (B1 F2, F14; B5 F16, F20)
Irish Election Literature, its partner on Snapshots of Political Action (B1 F9)

the organisations whose documents it holds (the Communist Party of Ireland, the Socialist Workers' Party, the Irish Republican Socialist Party, The Leninist group (CPGB), the Communist Party of Great Britain (Provisional Central Committee) among them), some of which are also its donors (B7 F37)
the Irish Labour History Society and its journal Saothar (B2 F41)
the Irish Republican Digital Archive, named beside it in Wikipedia's Sinn Féin article (B8.txt, search snippet; not ledgered)
Cork LGBT Archive, whose work on copyright in community digital archives the Copyright page thanks (B6; not ledgered)

the census's neighbours on the same page (the Marxists Internet Archive, the Encyclopedia of anti-Revisionism On-Line, the Amiel Melburn Trust Archive, libcom.org's collections), each a /non row being built the same day by other composers; no path is cited here

captures.description: THE ARCHIVE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'The Irish Left Archive is a digital project and online repository dedicated to collecting, preserving, and sharing material related to left-wing politics, activism, and history in Ireland.' Digital collection; timeline; scope; personal accounts; the podcast. Four cards: the archive, Spotify, Pocket Casts, mastodon.online.

atoms.evidence: The Irish Left Archive is a digital project and online repository
dedicated to collecting, preserving, and sharing material related to left-wing politics, activism, and history in Ireland.
Holds over 1,200 documents, hundreds of organizations, publications, profiles, and collections
Collects first-hand observations and reminiscences from activists and participants in Irish left movements.
Freely accessible documents, manifestos, pamphlets, and publications
